errors.text: The proposed Lomer-Cottrell lock unlocking, brittle HCP-pathway formation, and shear-induced amorphization cascade is not established by the target results or the cited evidence.

HCP atoms identified by CNA are treated as proof of a bulk FCC-to-HCP martensitic phase transformation, although in FCC indentation simulations they commonly represent local stacking faults or twin boundaries.
The claim that stacking-fault annihilation promotes increasing HCP content is mechanistically inconsistent unless an independent transformation pathway is demonstrated.

The cited evidence concerns CoNiCrFeMn nanowires under tensile deformation, not FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu under indentation and friction, so it does not validate the specific high-temperature mechanism or quantitative thresholds.
